The verdict is **fix**. The report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/24/session-7c6c8d93/minion-tracking-perf/review.md`. I made no code edits. The background search I started earlier finished, but I had already found the brief another way, so its result doesn't matter.

The task folder had no `requirements.md`. I checked the work against the brief in the spawn prompt, which I found in the minion's own transcript (session `b82c81af`).

**What must change:**
1. **The answer only exists in chat.** The minion's main finding is: 4–13 ms per write when the item tool runs inside the script, but 4,816 ms for the first write over Servex HTTP, then 48 and 42 ms. That is not in any committed file. It should go into the tracking readme with its date and branch.
2. **Two of the three layers were never measured.** The brief asked to time the item write path, the page tail (`live()`/follow) and the browser loading a page. `Server/JsonlPerf.mjs` only times the first.
3. **The fast timing is a floor, not the real cost.** When the item tool runs inside the script, Servex's hooks are not set up, so it skips the extra work the brief suspected. It also ran on the deputy's already-fixed branch, not the code that took 60 s. The readme and the page should label it that way.

**Notes (worth a look, not blocking):**
- The scratch folder path has a hard-coded date (`sessions/2026/10/24/`). On another day it creates folders it never removes.
- The prompt-coverage check re-reads the whole `prompts.jsonl` once per prompt.
- The new page sections were never opened in a browser. No screenshots came with this review, so their layout is unchecked.

**What was met:** check 4 (prompt coverage) and check 5 (JSONL timing with the 200 ms and 2 s flags) are both on the existing tracking page. The readme is updated, and it explains the "155 vs 123" count: neither number matches anything in the records.

1. **The timing numbers aren't saved anywhere.** The answer to "where the 60 s goes" is only in the minion's chat reply. Each write took 4–13 ms with the item tool running inside the script. Over Servex HTTP, the first write took 4,816 ms, then 48 and 42 ms. Those numbers should go into the tracking readme with the date and the branch.

- **The scratch folder path is hard-coded.** It is `sessions/2026/10/24/` inside the real site folder (`JsonlPerf.mjs:56`). On any other day the script leaves an empty date folder behind. Using the system temp folder would be simpler and is what the brief asked for.
- **The prompt check re-reads the whole prompt log once per prompt.** For big sessions this gets slow (`TrackingCheck.mjs:144`).
- **The tracking report is now slower to build.** Both new checks run on every run, and nobody has timed the cost.

The verdict is **fix**: one thing must change and five are notes. The report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/24/session-7c6c8d93/minion-tracking-perf/review.md`. I made no code edits.

The task folder had no `requirements.md`. I checked the work against the two briefs in the minions' own transcripts: the original one, and the follow-up written after the first review said fix. The diff includes the follow-up's fixes.

**Must change:**
- **The reason for not using the temp folder is wrong.** The readme and `Server/JsonlPerf.mjs:56` say the scratch copy for the item-write test can't go in the system temp folder, because the item tool only writes under `public/`. But `Servex/agents/page_tools.js:12` reads a `SERVEX_PUBLIC` setting meant for exactly this: pointing the tool's writes at a scratch folder. Setting it to a temp folder does what both briefs asked and makes the readme true.

**Worth a look:**
- **The main question isn't answered in writing.** Nothing says that no measured step came near 60 s. The worst was 4.8 s, on the first write through Servex. Every number was also taken on the branch that already has the deputy's fast-write fix, so the 60 s was never reproduced. One sentence in the readme would say so.
- **The coverage check can pick a different record than the existing tool.** When two prompt records have the same text, the new code in `TrackingCheck.mjs:155` keeps the last one, while `PromptRecords.rid()` keeps the first.
- **The readme's counts no longer match the page.** For session e00f55c9 the readme gives 111 unique prompts, all with refinements. The page now shows 122, with 97 refined, because the session kept growing after the backfill.
- **Two layers are only partly measured.** The page's live update after a write wasn't timed, and the browser number covers only fetching and parsing the file. The readme says both plainly, which the brief allowed.
- **I couldn't check the layout.** No screenshots came with this review. The minion says it opened the page at 1280 and 3440 wide and fixed two column overlaps.

**Met:** the timing script, three timed writes through Servex, the two new checks on the existing tracking page (prompt coverage, and JSONL read/write time flagged over 200 ms and 2 s), and the readme updates. The readme also explains the "155 vs 123" count: neither number matches anything in the records. The report run now reads each session's prompt records once instead of once per prompt, which brought it from 40–65 s down to about 35 s.

The report has only the Requirements and Words sections. The page-design sections need screenshots to answer.

**Verdict: pass, with 6 notes.** The report is at `minion-tracking-perf/review.md`.

There was no `requirements.md` in the task folder, so I took the brief from the minion's original spawn prompt in its transcript. I reviewed the branch head, b92e334a8.

**What works**
- `Server/JsonlPerf.mjs` does what the brief asked. I ran it against the main checkout's records: it printed the table and the verdict line, and three in-process item writes took 27–48 ms. It left nothing behind in the sessions folder.
- Checks 4 (prompt coverage) and 5 (JSONL perf) are in `Server/TrackingCheck.mjs`, `TrackingView.js` and the readme. It reuses `PromptRecords`, and the report shows 97 of 122 prompts covered across 18 sessions.
- The 155 vs 123 count is explained as far as the records allow: the readme says those numbers match nothing in them.
- All three changed files pass `node --check`.

**Notes worth a look**
- **The diff I was given is stale.** It stops one commit short of the head, at a version where `TrackingCheck.mjs` would crash with a ReferenceError. The head commit fixes that, so judge the branch, not the patch.
- **Merge, don't cherry-pick.** On the branch as it stands, `JsonlPerf.mjs --item` writes a probe record into the real sessions folder and never deletes it, because the branch's copy of `page_tools.js` ignores the scratch-folder setting. michael/dev's copy has the fix, so a merge is safe. A one-line guard in `JsonlPerf.mjs` would make it safe everywhere.
- **The "where do the 60 s go" question is still open.** Nothing measured came close: the worst write was 4.8 s, and every number was taken on code that already has the fast-write fix. The readme says this honestly. The way to actually reproduce it is to time the owner's own record on the commit before the fix.
- **The 4.8 s HTTP write is only in the readme.** `report.json` doesn't have it, so the page's "slowest write seen" understates what was measured.
- **The wrong record was timed.** `--item` measured the largest session file (397 KB), not the 186 KB record the owner named.
- **The page layout is unchecked.** I had no screenshots.
